question: Can a nonidentity translation between two separately defined propositional languages preserve formal derivations, open contexts and meaning in every Kripke world?
scope: Source IPC to a richer target syntax and natural-deduction calculus, with atoms mapped to their conjunction with truth. Proves proof/context transport and equivalence of Kripke forcing for every model/world, plus a syntactic non-surjectivity witness. Conservative encoding within Lean, not a semantic separation of foundations.

variants.statement: Source IPC derivations transport to the expanded formula calculus with translated assumptions
variants.construction: Induction on all source inference rules; explicit set-image transport

variants.statement: Target forcing of translate φ iff source forcing of φ at every world
variants.construction: Structural recursion; arbitrary persistent Kripke models

variants.statement: Satisfaction of translated premise images iff satisfaction of source context
variants.construction: Equivalence of every source assumption with its translation

variants.statement: No source formula maps to primitive target top syntax
variants.construction: Constructor distinction proves a concrete non-surjectivity claim about syntax

variants.statement: Translated derivation remains valid after composing with target identity interpretation
